rationale: Substantival use of ⲃⲱϣ 'be naked, stripped' (Lyc ⲃⲱⲱϣ). Central technical term of this kephalaion organizing the twelve-stripping chain: each defilement's 'nakedness' = what stands revealed when its outer covering is stripped away. The 'nakedness' of one defilement IS the next defilement in the chain. Direct Manichaean correspondential register.

ⲕⲱⲕ 'strip' + ⲁⲍⲏⲩ 'naked' (already in glossary as ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ 'strip naked'). Reaffirmed here as the iterative cosmological action by which fire, light, and tree successively strip the elements/defilements down through twelve stages. Substantival ⲡⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ = 'the stripping naked' (the act/event).

Greek loanword ῥεῦμα 'stream, flow, flux.' Lyc ⲍ-onset for Greek ῥ- (rough breathing). Used in this kephalaion (line 19) for the welling-flow of stripped defilement, identified with desire (ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ). Standard medical/cosmological loanword.

Likely Lyc reflex of Coptic ⲱⲕⲙ 'be sad, gloomy, defiled' (Crum 522b). Substantival 'the gloom/uncleanness' — the negative-affective state revealed when flesh is stripped. Position in the twelve-stripping chain: flesh → gloom → severity. Confidence moderate.

Tentatively read as Lyc 3pl conjunctive ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ- + ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix, here reduced to ⲡ̄?). Construction ⲛⲥⲉⲡ̄ ⲟⲩⲕⲓⲛⲇⲩⲛⲟⲥ 'and they become a danger' fits standard Coptic 'they make/become X.' Confidence low.

Demonstrative ⲡⲓ- + ⲡⲉⲧ- (relative qualitative) + ⲭⲱⲍⲙⲉ (Lyc ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ 'be defiled,' in glossary as ⲡⲧⲭⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'the defilement'). Substantival 'this defiled-one' — names the elements as defiled-bearers descending into the body. The whole chapter exposits how the fire/light/tree successively strip this defiled one's coverings.

ϩⲁ appears multiple times around the chapter heading (line 3 alone; line 5 start and end) without forming a coherent word in context. Treated as a decorative/section marker analogous to the >· ·< glyphs in page headers. Preserved transliterated but not translated as a word.
